facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus
who worked as a butcher and occasional hunter and had contact with hares and rabbits
lesions on left hand evolving over 3 days
vesiculobullous lesions appeared on the dorsal aspect of his left hand and extended into the web space between the first and second fingers
the lesion extended to the palm and ventral aspect of the thumb with an eroded area on which pustules appeared
No fever or other systemic symptoms were present
Hemorrhagic bullous lesions on the dorsal aspect of left hand extending to web space between first and second fingers
Surface erosion with pustular lesions on palm and ventral aspect of thumb
Fungal culture was negative
bacterial culture showed Staphylococcus simulans
Polymerase chain reaction analysis for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae was negative
Initially hemorrhagic bullous lesions appeared

concepts.why: The patient has lesions on the left hand and the bacterial culture showed Staphylococcus simulans, which suggests a Staphylococcal skin infection.
The patient had contact with hares and rabbits and presented with lesions on the left hand, which could be consistent with cutaneous erysipeloid, a zoonotic disease.
The patient presented with vesiculobullous lesions on the dorsal aspect of the left hand, which is consistent with a vesiculobullous dermatosis.
The patient has surface erosion with pustular lesions on the palm and ventral aspect of the thumb, which could be consistent with pyoderma, a type of skin infection.
The patient presented with lesions on the left hand and had contact with hares and rabbits, which could be consistent with contact dermatitis.
The patient has lesions on the left hand and the bacterial culture showed Staphylococcus simulans, which could be consistent with impetigo, a highly contagious skin infection.
The patient presented with hemorrhagic bullous lesions and surface erosion with pustular lesions, which could be consistent with cellulitis, a bacterial skin infection.
The patient presented with vesiculobullous lesions and the fungal culture was negative, which could be consistent with eczema herpeticum, a rare but serious skin condition.

The negative polymerase chain reaction analysis for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae rules out Erysipeloid, but the patient's occupation and contact with animals, along with the nature of the lesions, could have suggested it.
